neet_che_u04_t01_1.working: Temperature does not depend on the amount of matter, so it is intensive. Volume, enthalpy and mass all scale with amount, so they are extensive.

neet_che_u04_t01_2.working: Density, temperature and molar heat capacity are intensive. Gibbs energy, entropy and heat capacity all scale with amount, so option 4 contains only extensive properties.

neet_che_u04_t01_3.working: Density and temperature are intensive, so they stay ρ and T. Heat capacity is extensive, so it halves to C/2.

neet_che_u04_t01_4.working: Density = mass/volume (III). Molar heat capacity = C/n (IV). Molar volume = V/n (I). Heat capacity is extensive and is shared between the halves (II).

neet_che_u04_t01_5.working: A is true: a ratio of extensives (e.g., mass/volume) is intensive. B is true. C is false because E° is intensive. D is true. E is false because surface tension and viscosity are intensive. So A, B and D.
